A new output panel, bit-perfect playback on Linux, and volume control for DACs in bit-perfect mode. Queue settings, with presets that work like Apple Music or Spotify. And fixes for a macOS bug where a DAC could stay unusable by other apps after Ond played to it.

### Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `Ond-0.4.0-macos-universal.dmg` (or `.zip`) | macOS 11 or later, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `Ond-0.4.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux on x86_64, glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, Debian 13) |
| `Ond-0.4.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Linux on ARM64, same requirements |
| `Ond-0.4.0-windows-x86_64.zip` | Windows 10 and 11. Still untested on real hardware; issues welcome. |

On NixOS or with Nix: `nix profile install github:Solidsilver/ond/v0.4.0`. Install steps for every platform are in the [README](https://github.com/Solidsilver/ond#install).

### Output

- The device name in the toolbar is now the device's icon, beside the volume. Click it for the output panel.
- The panel has two modes. System output plays wherever your computer plays. Choose a device picks one, and devices that can play bit-perfect get a switch for it.
- In bit-perfect mode the volume slider sets the DAC's own volume, so the samples Ond sends stay untouched. A green dot in the slider's knob shows this. The panel shows the exact level in dB, steps it by 0.5 dB with the arrow keys, and has a mute button.
- Bit-perfect playback on Linux. Ond asks PipeWire to release the card, plays to it directly, and hands it back a few seconds after playback stops.
- If the device you chose is unplugged, Ond plays through the system output and switches back when it returns.
- Settings › Output lists devices in groups. You can make your own groups and hide devices from the panel.
- Optional notice when the output device changes (Settings › Output, off by default).

### Bit-perfect fixes

- macOS: Ond puts a device's sample rate and format back the way it found them after playback stops and when you quit. A DAC that another app, or an earlier version of Ond, left unusable is fixed when Ond starts.
- Bit-perfect is opt-in for every device, and only offered where it works: DACs, HDMI and other outputs that take the file's samples as they are. Speakers, Bluetooth, AirPlay and software devices always play shared.
- macOS: bit-perfect on USB DACs like the Behringer UMC22 plays again. It was silent while showing "Verified".
- macOS: with the DAC as the system default, turning on bit-perfect no longer makes playback stop and start over and over.
- Normal mode leaves the device at its own sample rate and Ond converts the rate, like other music players. To have the device follow each song's rate instead, turn on Settings › Output › Match each song's sample rate (macOS).

### Queue

- Play next puts songs at the top of the queue. It used to put them at the end.
- Settings › Queue sets where Play next and Add to queue put songs, what playing something new does with songs you added, and what Clear removes. Presets match Ond, Apple Music and Spotify. By default, songs you added keep playing after the new music.
- Right-click a split "You added" group to bring its songs back together.

### Smaller fixes

- Linux: the now-playing display is centered when the window buttons are on the right.
- Quitting waits for the audio engine to release the output device.
